full_judgment:
Krishna Debnath J. This Criminal Appeal arises out of leave granted by this court on 06.08.2009 in Criminal Petition for leave to Appeal No. 569 012008 directed against the judgment and order passed on 16th June 2008 by the High Court Division in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.6053 of 2008 filed by the accused-respondent under Section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and made the Rule absolute quashing the proceeding of Dhanmondi Police Station Case No.48 dated 25.03.2008 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 254 of 2008 under section 409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 pending before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Dhaka. 

 2. The facts involved in this case, in short, are that one Md. Moniruzzaman Khan, Deputy Director of Anti-Corruption Commission, Head Office, Dhaka as informant lodged an FIR with the Dhanmondi Police Station stating, inter-alia, that while he :was enquiring into various matters arising out of corruption relating to Rural Power Company Limited, considered various records relating to purchase of goods locally for the period from August, 2005 to December, 2005 and found that Md. Zahirul Islam Khan, former Managing Director-in-Charge of the said company, during his tenure , for the purpose of taking over Mymensingh Power Plant has taken various amounts through various cheques totaling tk. 58,40,197.00 as advance for meeting up the expenditure of the said takeover, that alter getting the said advance, he has filed vouchers of different dates related to the expenditures which have been approved by him and later the accounts department has coordinated it by journal voucher, that during enquiry it has inspired that several expenditures are not correct and thus money has been misappropriated by showing fake expenditures; that in fact the personal officer, Aminul Islam has not taken money from the Managing Director and he has not purchased any goods as have been shown; that it seems that the Managing Director-in Charge of Rural Power Company Limited has misappropriated tk. 8,37,7820.00 by showing false and fake expenditures. 

 4. That having .failed in the Writ, accused respondents invoked inherent power of the High Court Division under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and filed Criminal Miscellaneous Petition grounding inter-alia that (1) there is no ingredients of Section 409 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, for expenditure was post facto approved by the resolution of the company thus the HR was preposterous and the accused respondents are not public servants (I1) for harassing the accuseds (III) paying of tk. 19,44,600.00 to the law firm as fees for conducting writ petition cannot be regarded as misappropriation. 

 Limited having Government interest of 410(41%) paid up shares through REB out of 1000 total paid up shares, and as the Merchant as well and bundle of facts dis-closed prima facie offences under Section 409 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947; (11) there being no proceedings existing the abuse of the process is absent under law and bundle of facts disclosing the offences alleged cannot be quashed under both the statutory and Court Jurisprudence, the impugned Judgment and order dated .16.6.2008 of quashing the FIR of Dhanmondi Police Station Case No. 48 (03)2008 corresponding to CSR No.254 of 2008 and stopping of ongoing statutory investigation under Section 17 of ACC is to be set aside as not maintainable allowing the investigation and trial to continue to its natural end. 

 8. Mr. Aziz Khan, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant submits that the respondent is a public servant as Milled in C1.12(b) of the Section 21 of the Penal Code that reads that "Every person in the service or pay of a local authority or a corporation, body or authority established by or under any law or of a firm or company in which any part of the interest or share capital is held by or vested on the Government" inasmuch as 410 out of 1000 paid up shares are held by REB. The Section 409 of the Penal Code as such is applicable and also applicable to be altered during trial. For there is legal evidence and the FIR discloses offence alleged, inherent power available under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure needs not be invoked to interfere the trial in this ease which the High Court Division failed to take into consideration and passed the impugned judgment and order occasioning a serious failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the accused-respondent embezzled an amount of tk 27,82,620.00 of Rural Power Company Limited through unauthorized voucher and committed offence under Section 409 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, the High Court Division miserably failed to take this important aspect into consideration and passed the impugned judgment and order occasioning a serious miscarriage of justice which is not at all sustain-able in law. 

 13. In the case of Abdul (Nader and other vs. State, 28 DLR (AD) 38 it has been observed by the Appellate Division that- 

 "A third category of cases in which the inherent jurisdiction of the High Court can he invoked may also arise. In cases falling under this category the allegations made against the accused person do constitute an offence alleged but there is either no legal evidence adduced in support of the case or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge. In dealing with this class of cases it is important to bear in mind the distinction between a case where there is no legal evidence or where there is evidence which is manifestly and clearly inconsistent with the accusation made and cases where there is legal evidence which on its appreciation may not support the accusation in question." 

 14. This being the legal position the question arises whether the present case falls under the category in which the inherent power of the High Court. Division be invoked or not. In the present case the High Court Division quashing the proceedings has exercised the power under Section 561 A occasioning serious mistakes as there appears no such situation where the High Court Division found in support of the case 'no legal evidence' or the evidence which was adduced clearly or manifestly failed to prove the charge against the accuseds. Additionally we think that there appears to be no legal bar to the institution of present proceedings or their continuation. 

 15. In view o the above discussions we found that the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.6053 of 2008 making the rule absolute quashing the proceeding of G.R. No.254 of 2008 arising out of Dhanmondi Police Station Case No.48 dated 25.03.2008 under Section 409 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 occasioned a miscarriage of justice. The High Court Division at so early stage by exercise of an extraordinary power which is given for the dispensation of complete justice granted an unfortunate fate for the present whole proceeding. 

 16. Here we may refer the case of Raja Hug Newaz v. Mohd. Afzal reported in 19 DIA (SC) 369 where it was held that- 

 "Quashing of proceedings at so early stage gives an unfortunate impression of stifling of criminal prosecution, by exercise of an extra ordinary power which is given for the dispensation of complete justice, in the forms provided by law. It is necessary that this case should be examined further, to ensure that the course of even handed justice is not prejudiced." 

 20. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is hereby set aside. The proceeding of G.R. No.254 of 2008 arising out of Dhanmondi Police Station Case No.48 dated 25.03.2008 shall continue in accordance with law.
